description: In the Sustainable Smart Parks project in Gothenburg, Sweden, new technologies such as multiple sensors, smartphones and internet-connected devices were applied and tested for their availability, reliability and relevance to contemporary management of urban green space. This article introduces an analytical framework based on urban ecology and nature-based thinking and uses it to examine the initiative, asking how smart technologies can make green space management more inclusive and effective. Coverage: parks in Gothenburg. Access: article on the journal site. Licence: not stated on the page read. Caveats: the evaluation is qualitative, and the authors call for testing the five criteria in wider contexts. Outcome: the framework worked in distinguishing how technologies integrate diversity, connectivity, adaptation, inclusion and perception, but a joint systems approach to future management has yet to be developed; the authors suggest coupling technologies that share a focus within each criterion. Simulation uses: designing sensor networks and data flows for park digital twins and maintenance. Related records: the IPPODAMO facility management digital twin and the Münster green space layer.
